samples.summary: New `--coderabbit-latency` path reaches a `gh api` endpoint built by string interpolation from unvalidated store data (`source_pr`, `review_commit`) — API path/query injection with the operator's GitHub credentials
samples.evidence: The diff adds a network read to the scorer CLI: `cost-latency.mjs:1088` calls `corpusRecords(store, args["corpus-version"])`. `corpusRecords` (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1142) passes the corpus manifest's `it.source_pr` straight into `fetchCodeRabbitPr`, which does only `String(pr ?? "").trim()` (line 1059) and then interpolates it into the request path: `repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/${n}/comments?per_page=100` (lines 1062/1070), plus `issues/${n}/comments` (1079). `it.review_commit` is likewise interpolated by `commitCheckRuns` into `repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits/${sha}/check-runs?per_page=100` (scripts/agent/gh-checks.mjs:131). The module already owns a validator for exactly this value — `codeRabbitItemId` refuses anything not `^\d+$` (line 322) — but it runs only *inside* `codeRabbitRecords` at line 1143, i.e. AFTER all five network calls have already been issued, so the gate does not protect the request path. `gh` is spawned with `execFileSync` (gh-checks.mjs:27) so there is no shell metacharacter risk, but an attacker who can write the eval-data root's `corpus/manifests/<v>.json` (a store deliberately held outside this repo and shared/synced between machines, per store.mjs:265-281) controls path segments and query string of an authenticated `api.github.com` request made by whoever runs the scorer — e.g. `"source_pr": "1/comments?per_page=1&x="` or `"../../../repos/other/private/issues"`. Same defect is directly demonstrable via the adapter's own CLI (`fetchCodeRabbitPr(args.pr)` at line 1267 runs before `codeRabbitItemId(args.pr)` at 1273), and no test asserts `fetchCodeRabbitPr` validates its argument. I could not confirm how `gh`/GitHub normalise `..` segments, so exploit depth is unproven; the missing pre-fetch validation is concrete. Fix: validate with `codeRabbitItemId`/`^\d+$` (and a `^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$` check on the sha) before the first API call.

samples.summary: Operator-facing text still claims the scorer spawns nothing / costs nothing, while the new flag spawns `gh` and makes authenticated network calls
samples.evidence: The diff rewrote the USAGE line to "Writes nothing and spawns nothing." (cost-latency.mjs:1011-1012), but `--coderabbit-latency` reaches `corpusRecords` → `fetchCodeRabbitPr` → `gh(...)` → `execFileSync("gh", args)` (scripts/agent/gh-checks.mjs:27): the tool now forks a subprocess and issues five authenticated GitHub API calls per corpus item using ambient `GH_TOKEN`/`gh auth` credentials. The module header at line 50 ("NOTHING IS WRITTEN AND NOTHING IS SPENT. It reads a store, computes, prints.") was likewise not updated to disclose the credentialed network read. A reader who trusts "spawns nothing" may run this in a context where an outbound authenticated request is not acceptable (e.g. against a corpus manifest of unknown provenance — see the injection finding above). The later paragraph does say the flag makes network calls, so this is a contradiction rather than a total omission.

samples.summary: Absence-flavour census is keyed by a data-derived string (`out[key].absent[s.absent] = …`), which the new report consumes; a `__proto__`/`toString` flavour is silently swallowed and arbitrary flavour text is interpolated into report lines
samples.evidence: The diff's `coderabbitLatency` stores `census: latencyCensus(perItem)` (cost-latency.mjs ~line 650) and `renderCoderabbitLatency` prints unrecognised keys verbatim as `UNRECOGNISED ${f}=${absent[f]}` (cost-latency.mjs:993), while `costLatencyOf` interpolates the same keys into `completeness.reasons` (the new `coderabbit latency:` reason). Those keys come from `latencyCensus`'s `out[key].absent[s.absent] = (out[key].absent[s.absent] ?? 0) + 1` (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1039), where `s.absent` is an arbitrary string from the record. With `s.absent === "__proto__"` the assignment hits the Object.prototype setter with a number, which is a silent no-op — the count is lost and `Object.keys` never shows it, defeating the "an unrecognised absence must appear as an unexplained bucket" property the surrounding comment claims; `"hasOwnProperty"`/`"toString"` would instead produce a count seeded from an inherited function. Newlines in a flavour string would also forge extra report lines. Reachable only from a hostile/crafted records source (the injected `coderabbit.latency` library option, or a tampered adapter), so exploitability is low; the hardening is `Object.create(null)` for the census maps plus rejecting flavours outside `LATENCY_ABSENT`.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as written. `fetchCodeRabbitPr` (adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1058-1059) normalises `pr` with only `String(pr ?? "").trim()` and interpolates the result into `gh api` request paths at lines 1062/1070/1079; `reviewCommit` flows unvalidated through line 1086 into `commitCheckRuns`, interpolated at gh-checks.mjs:131. `corpusRecords` calls `fetchCodeRabbitPr(it.source_pr, {reviewCommit: it.review_commit})` at line 1142, one line BEFORE `codeRabbitRecords` (1143) which is the only thing that eventually reaches the `^\d+$` refusal in `codeRabbitItemId` (320-323, used at 541) — so the validator runs after all five network calls, exactly as claimed. No upstream guard exists: `EvalStore.getCorpusManifest`/`getCorpus` (store.mjs:751-766) JSON.parse the manifest and return `m.items` with no shape validation, and the SHA40 check at store.mjs:436 covers only item meta writes, not manifest entries. The new `--coderabbit-latency` reachability is real (cost-latency.mjs:1025 flag, 1087-1088 call). The `--pr` CLI path demonstrates the same ordering (fetch at 1267, validation at 1273). `gh` is spawned via execFileSync (gh-checks.mjs:27) so there is no shell injection, but path/query segments of an authenticated api.github.com request remain attacker-controllable by anyone who can write the external eval-data root's manifest. In-lane (injection / unsafe input handling), no named refutation ground available.
